name: SkipLink
summary: The first link of a page. Hidden until it takes keyboard focus, then Enter moves focus past the header and navigation to the main content.
useWhen: Every page that has a header, a navigation or other blocks repeated before its main content (WCAG 2.4.1)
A long region a keyboard user may want to jump past, such as a search panel or a footer, with one extra link per target
An app shell: PageShell renders it first
avoidWhen: Navigation between sections of the same article, which readers use with a pointer too
A link that must always be visible
A page with no repeated block before the main content

href.description: The fragment of the element to jump to. The target is found by id.

children.description: The visible text. Under an Arabic Theme the default is الانتقال للمحتوى الرئيسي.

a11y.focus: Placed first in body, it is the first tab stop of the page. Visually hidden at rest, drawn at the block start and inline start corner on focus, with a 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring on keyboard focus.

keys.Tab: Moves focus to the skip link from the top of the page, which draws it
keys.Enter: Moves focus to the target and scrolls it into view

a11y.announce: The link text is the accessible name. After Enter, the screen reader reads the target from the start.
notes: WCAG 2.4.1 Bypass blocks.

The target gets tabindex -1 only when focus does not land on it as it is. A link, a button, a field or an element with its own tabindex keeps what it has; an anchor with no href or a disabled control gets tabindex -1.
Focus moves to the target itself, not only the scroll position, so the next Tab continues from the main content in every browser.

The URL fragment changes after focus moves, so hashchange and :target fire as for a plain fragment link. A click with a modifier key or a middle click is left to the browser. When the target is missing the browser handles the link.
Drawn on any focus, keyboard or pointer, so it never vanishes under the pointer that clicked it. At 24px or more tall when shown (WCAG 2.5.8).
Under forced colors it is drawn in LinkText on Canvas with a LinkText border, and the focus outline uses Highlight.
No native title attribute.

en.label: Skip to plus the place: Skip to main content, Skip to search. Sentence case.
en.many: One link per target, in the order the targets appear on the page.

ar.label: Noun form, no diacritics: الانتقال للمحتوى الرئيسي، الانتقال للبحث.

react.behavior: native a, focus moved by hand
react.note: No motion: the link appears at once on focus, so there is no pattern to name and nothing to reduce.

angular.behavior: a[dsSkipLink], host bindings, a click handler that moves focus

native.note: Native screen readers move by headings and containers, and there is no tab order to bypass. Start the first content block with a heading (accessibilityRole header on its title) so screen reader users can jump to it.

styles.studio: A surface-3 pill with bright text, a control border and the menu shadow.
styles.desk: The same look from the Desk tokens, on a solid surface so it reads over any backdrop.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: A skip link with display none at rest
mistakes.right: SkipLink, which stays in the tab order and the accessibility tree while hidden

mistakes.wrong: A skip link that only scrolls, so the next Tab starts from the header again
mistakes.right: SkipLink, which moves focus to the target

mistakes.wrong: tabindex 0 on the main region so it can take focus
mistakes.right: Nothing: the skip link adds tabindex -1 when it is needed, which keeps the region out of the tab order

mistakes.wrong: A skip link placed after the navigation
mistakes.right: The first element in body

name: TableOfContents
summary: Links to the headings of a long page, nested by level, with the section in view marked as the reader scrolls.
useWhen: A long document, guide or settings page with four or more sections a reader may jump between
A docs page with a side column that can hold a sticky list of its sections
A page where readers need to see which section they are in while they scroll
avoidWhen: A short page with one or two sections
Switching between separate views or pages, rather than sections of one page
Navigation of the whole site or app

items.description: The headings of the page in document order: { id, label, level }. They nest by level through buildTree in @the-system/shared; a skipped level nests one step down.

title.description: The visible title, a p that names the nav through aria-labelledby. Under an Arabic Theme the default is محتوى الصفحة. false hides it; then pass aria-label.

size.description: Type size: sm is font.size.xs, md font.size.s, one step up in Arabic. Every link is at least 24px tall.

offset.description: The height of a sticky header above the content, in px. A heading counts as reached when its top passes this line plus a fifth of the viewport, at most 64px (the reading line).

sticky.description: Keeps the list in view as the page scrolls (position sticky, below offset plus space.l), scrolls inside when taller than dialog.height.max, and keeps the active link in view inside the list without scrolling the page. Sets data-sticky.

active.description: The active heading id, controlled. Default: tracked from the scroll position.

onActiveChange.description: Called when the active heading changes, from scrolling or a link.

a11y.role: navigation landmark named by its title, with ordered lists of links
a11y.focus: Each link is a tab stop. Enter or a click moves focus to the heading itself (tabindex -1 only when the heading is not focusable), so the next Tab continues from that section. A 2px ring from focus.shadow.ring.

keys.Enter: Scrolls to the heading and moves focus to it

a11y.announce: Navigation, On this page, list. The link of the section in view reads as current location (aria-current location). The indicator is aria-hidden.
notes: The section in view is marked by medium weight, the indicator bar and aria-current location, never color alone (WCAG 1.4.1).
Items carry data-level (1, 2, 3 and deeper) for their nesting depth, which sets the indent. It is not listed under states because it holds a number, not an empty boolean.

Scrolling is smooth, and a jump under prefers-reduced-motion. The URL fragment is set with history.pushState, so there is no second jump; hashchange does not fire and :target does not update. While the scroll plays, sections passed on the way are not marked; scrollend lifts the hold.
A click with a modifier key or a middle click is left to the browser.

The active section comes from activeHeading in @the-system/shared at the reading line (offset plus a fifth of the viewport, at most 64px). An IntersectionObserver on that line and the scrollend event trigger a new measure, once per frame at most; nothing runs on every scroll event. A ResizeObserver keeps the indicator on its link when the list reflows.

Sticky form (WCAG 2.4.11): the list sits below offset plus space.l and keeps scroll padding around the active link. Give the headings scroll-margin-block-start equal to any sticky page header and pass the same height as offset, so a heading never lands under the header.
Under forced colors the indicator uses Highlight and the focus outline uses Highlight.
On load, the section named by the URL fragment is marked first, when there is one.

en.title: On this page, or a title that names the document: In this guide.
en.labels: The heading text as written on the page, sentence case. Shorten only when the heading is longer than a line.

ar.title: محتوى الصفحة, noun form, no diacritics.
ar.labels: The heading text as on the page. Each link text has dir auto, so a Latin term or name keeps its own direction.

react.behavior: nav with ol of anchors; IntersectionObserver in an effect; buildTree and activeHeading from @the-system/shared
react.note: The indicator moves with a transform transition (tab-indicator); under reduced motion the duration is 0ms and the scroll is a jump.

angular.behavior: nav[dsTableOfContents] with the shared buildTree and activeHeading, IntersectionObserver in afterNextRender

native.note: A list of pressables that scroll a ScrollView to measured section offsets with scrollTo; onScroll feeds activeHeading.

styles.studio: A hairline rail at the inline start, muted links that brighten on hover, a bright bar beside the section in view.
styles.desk: The same from the Desk tokens.
styles.neutral: Takes the tokens of the Neutral style, no recipe.

mistakes.wrong: The section in view marked by color only
mistakes.right: TableOfContents, which adds weight, the bar and aria-current location

mistakes.wrong: Links that only scroll, so the next Tab starts from the list again
mistakes.right: TableOfContents, which moves focus to the heading

mistakes.wrong: A scroll listener that measures every heading on every frame
mistakes.right: The IntersectionObserver in TableOfContents and activeHeading

mistakes.wrong: Headings that land under a sticky header after a jump
mistakes.right: scroll-margin-block-start on the headings and the same height as offset

name: Theme
summary: Stamps every runtime axis on its own element, resolves what is not passed from the nearest parent Theme, and gives the subtree its direction, icon set and style data.
useWhen: At the root of an app, once, so tokens, base CSS, direction and icons apply
Around a subtree that needs another scheme, style, density, language or direction
Around a demo or a preview that shows one combination of axes
avoidWhen: Changing one color or size in one place: use a component prop or a token
Setting dir or lang alone on an element: the tokens, Radix and the icons would not follow
Wrapping every component: one Theme per subtree that changes an axis is enough

style.description: The style pack id. Any custom id is accepted. At the root the default is studio; nested, the parent's.

scheme.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested. A scheme the style does not list falls back to its default.

density.description: Default from the style.json at the root, the parent's when nested.

glass.description: Read only by styles that use glass.

dir.description: Follows lang when lang is passed and dir is not. Otherwise the parent's, then from lang.

lang.description: A BCP 47 tag. The system ships en and ar.

css.description: Inline styles for the Theme element, as a React style object. style is taken by the style axis.

a11y.focus: Never focusable. It adds no role.
notes: dir and lang on the element let screen readers pick the right voice and let CSS mirror the layout.
The Radix direction provider follows dir, so menus, sliders and arrow keys mirror in right to left.
Arabic text gets IBM Plex Sans Arabic, zero tracking, taller lines and small text one step up through base.css. Body text keeps its size.

A root Theme is needed even when <html> is stamped with themeAttributes(): attributes give the CSS its axes but no React context, so useTheme, useOptionalPart and the Dialog and Toaster portals would fall back to the root defaults (Studio dark, English). Stamp <html> for the first paint and wrap the app in <Theme> with the same axes.

en.lang: Set lang on the root Theme. A Latin island inside Arabic is any element with lang en; it gets the Latin type back.

ar.lang: Set lang ar on the root Theme. dir follows as rtl.

react.note: Exports Theme, useTheme, useOptionalPart, themeAttributes and resolveTheme from packages/react/src/theme. themeAttributes() on <html> does not replace the root <Theme>: attributes carry no React context.

angular.note: dsTheme directive in packages/angular/src/theme, inputs named like the React props. A static style="desk" never reaches the style input (the Angular compiler parses it as inline CSS): bind [style]="'desk'" or use dsTheme="desk". Inline styles pass through css. Provides DsThemeService (value signal, optionalPart), the CDK Directionality and the icon style to its subtree. applyDocumentTheme stamps the html element.

native.note: ThemeProvider passes the resolved theme object through context, with the same axis names.

styles.studio: Black body, Inter Variable, default density
styles.desk: Black desk, Instrument Sans, default density, window and dialog controls and titlebar turned on

mistakes.wrong: <div dir="rtl" lang="ar"> around a screen
mistakes.right: <Theme lang="ar">, which also sets dir, the Radix direction and the Arabic type

mistakes.wrong: <Theme style={{ padding: 8 }}>
mistakes.right: <Theme css={{ padding: 8 }}>: style is the style axis

mistakes.wrong: Reading data-style from the DOM to pick a branch
mistakes.right: useTheme().style, or useOptionalPart for a part only one style shows

mistakes.wrong: <html {...themeAttributes({ style: "desk", lang: "ar" })}> with no Theme around the app
mistakes.right: Stamp <html> and also wrap the app in <Theme style="desk" lang="ar">: portals and useTheme read the React context, not the html attributes

name: TitleBar
summary: The bar at the top of a window or a panel: window controls at the start, the title, then trailing actions.
useWhen: The header of a Window, or of a Dialog drawn as a window in Desk
A panel header that needs a title and a close button
avoidWhen: The header of a page
A toolbar of many tools with no title

title.description: The title. One line with an ellipsis.

titleId.description: id of the title, for aria-labelledby on the window or dialog.

actions.description: The end slot: IconButtons and small Buttons.

moveLabel.description: Puts the title in a focusable move handle (part move, role group) named by this label: "Move window". The host (Window) listens for the keys there.

moveHint.default: Arrow keys move the window. Shift moves it further.
moveHint.description: Description of the move handle, through aria-describedby. Under lang="ar" the default is مفاتيح الأسهم لتحريك النافذة، ومع Shift لمسافة أبعد.

a11y.role: none: a plain container. The title is a heading (h2 by default).
a11y.focus: The bar itself is not focusable. With moveLabel the move handle is a tab stop with the 2px ring; while it has keyboard focus the title wraps to show in full. Then the controls and actions take focus in order.

keys.Tab: Moves through the controls, the move handle and the actions

a11y.announce: The heading is read in document order. A window or dialog points aria-labelledby at titleId.
notes: The title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text stays in the DOM, and keyboard focus on the move handle shows it wrapped.
Parts minimize, zoom and close are IconButtons a host renders in the actions slot when it has no lights (Window in Studio). They belong to the TitleBar, their nearest root.
In right to left layouts a bar with controls keeps them at the top left and centers the title, as macOS draws it. A bar without controls mirrors.

en.title: A file or app name in sentence case.

ar.title: Noun form, no diacritics. Latin file names go through Bidi.

angular.note: A first port exists for the Desk dialog chrome (packages/angular/src/components/title-bar): controls, title (a string, a TemplateRef or an ng-template dsTitleBarTitle), actions, as, titleId, active, with the React DOM. No move handle and no demo yet; it turns ready with Window. TitleBar.css is used as is.

native.note: Native screens use the platform navigation bar.

styles.studio: A plain header on the panel surface with a hairline under it (recipes/Window.css when inside a Window).
styles.desk: Transparent, as the source .dwin-bar: the window glass shows through, no divider. The lights sit at the start.

mistakes.wrong: A title in a native title attribute to show the full text
mistakes.right: The full text stays in the title; a Tooltip shows it

mistakes.wrong: Mirroring the lights in Arabic
mistakes.right: The lights keep their place and order; only a bar without lights mirrors

name: Toast
summary: A short notice that something happened, shown in a corner and gone on its own. Called from anywhere with toast(); one Toaster renders them. Call shape: toast(title, options) or toast(options); toast.success, toast.warning, toast.danger and toast.info set the tone; each returns the id; toast.dismiss(id) closes one (or all, without an id), toast.update(id, patch) changes one in place, toast.configure(config) sets the max and the durations for the app.
useWhen: Confirming that an action the person took has finished: Draft saved, Link copied
A failure the person can fix later or retry from the toast, as tone danger with one action
A background event worth knowing now: a new version, a finished upload
Progress that ends in a result, updated in place with toast.update
avoidWhen: The person needs to make a decision before going on
Long content, a list, or anything to read twice
A critical error that blocks the task or loses data
A message tied to one field or one place on the page
Something that must stay on screen while the condition lasts

parts.Toast: root, without behavior and without data-state
parts.isInsideToaster: helper for overlays: true for a target inside the toaster

tone.description: The color and icon, and the timing: neutral, info and success close after 4s, warning after 6s, danger stays until closed.

title.description: One line: what happened, naming the thing.

description.description: More detail. Long text wraps in full; keep it to one or two sentences.

duration.description: toast() option. Milliseconds before it closes; Infinity keeps it. Default by tone. Ignored for danger and for a toast with an action, which stay until closed. toast.configure({ durations, max }) lengthens them for the whole app.

action.description: toast() option. One button: { label, onAction, altText }. A toast with an action never times out. altText is read in place of the button, for example where else the same action lives.

dedupeKey.description: toast() option. A toast that reads the same as an open one bumps its count instead of stacking; a key groups repeats with other copy; false turns it off.

id.description: toast() option. A call with the id of an open toast updates it.

lang.description: toast() option. The language of the copy when it differs from the page. The root gets lang and dir.

count.description: Toast prop. The repeat count; the Toaster passes it from the store.

onClose.description: Toast prop. Renders the close button and is called by it. The Toaster always renders it.

closeLabel.description: The accessible name of the close button. Arabic under lang ar.

position.description: Toaster prop. end is the inline end: right in English, left in Arabic.

label.description: Toaster prop. The name of the region. {hotkey} in it is replaced by the hotkey.

hotkey.description: Toaster prop. The keys that move focus to the toasts.

store.description: Toaster prop. The store to render. Default the app wide store behind toast().

a11y.role: The Toaster is a region (named Notifications) holding a list; each toast is a list item. Announcements go through two visually hidden regions owned by the Toaster: role status (polite) and role alert (assertive, for danger).
a11y.focus: Not modal: toasts never take focus on their own. F8 moves focus to the list, which shows the focus ring; Tab moves through the toasts, newest first, and each toast's action and close button. Closing the focused toast puts focus on the list. While a dialog with a focus trap is open, keyboard focus stays in the dialog: the toasts stay visible, readable and clickable, and a toast with an action waits until the dialog closes.

keys.F8: Moves focus to the notifications list
keys.Tab: Moves to the next toast, action or close button
keys.Enter: Runs the focused action or close button
keys.Escape: Closes a toast only when the key comes from inside the toaster: the focused toast, or the newest one from the list. Escape anywhere else, in a Window, a Dialog or a form, leaves every toast alone, a danger toast included, and is not prevented, so the system Dialog still closes itself. A raw Radix Dialog from a consumer does not get that Escape while a toast shows above it (Radix gives Escape to the top layer only), so use the system Dialog or close the toast first.

a11y.announce: Once per change (WCAG 4.1.3): when a toast shows, and again on each repeat or update, as "Notification. Title. Description. Action alternative." with the toast's text in the toast's language. danger is assertive (role alert), the rest polite (role status). The toast itself has no live role and keeps its element across a repeat or update, so it is never read twice and focus stays. Radix's own announcer is muted. The close button is not read.
notes: danger toasts and toasts with an action stay until closed. The others pause while the pointer is over them, while focus is inside, and while the window is blurred or the tab hidden (WCAG 2.2.1). toast.configure({ durations }) lengthens them for the whole app.
Swipe toward the edge closes a toast; the close button is the button path for the same action (WCAG 2.5.7).

Above an open modal dialog the toasts stay visible (z.toast is above z.dialog), stay in the accessibility tree and take the pointer. A dialog calls isInsideToaster(event.target) in onFocusOutside, onPointerDownOutside and onInteractOutside and prevents the default, so a toast never closes it.
At most three toasts show at once; the rest wait their turn, so a burst never covers the page.
No native title attribute anywhere.

en.title: Say what happened and name the thing: Draft saved, Could not upload photo.jpg. Sentence case, no exclamation marks.
en.description: Optional. What it means or what to do next, in one or two short sentences. Long text wraps in full, so keep it short.
en.action: A verb plus a noun: Retry upload, Undo move, Open draft. Never OK, Continue, Confirm or Yes. One action at most. The toast then stays until closed.
en.danger: Name the failure and what is safe: Could not publish page. Your draft is safe.
en.repeats: Keep the copy the same for the same event, so repeats fold into one toast with a count.

ar.title: Say what happened and name the thing, in noun forms where you can: المسودة محفوظة، تعذر رفع الصورة. No diacritics.
ar.action: Noun form labels, no diacritics: إعادة الرفع، تراجع عن النقل. Never the imperative.
ar.digits: Western digits. Latin names in the copy go through Bidi when the toast is rendered by hand.
ar.lang: Pass lang: "ar" when the page is not Arabic, so the toast gets the Arabic type and direction.

react.note: Toaster renders the shared store from @the-system/shared; toast is re-exported from @the-system/react. Call shape: toast(title: string, options?) or toast(options) with title inside; toast.success, toast.warning, toast.danger and toast.info take the same arguments and set tone; toast.dismiss(id?), toast.update(id, { tone, title, description }), toast.configure({ max, durations }). From packages/shared/src/toast.ts.

angular.behavior: the shared toast store with cdk:a11y LiveAnnouncer
angular.note: Reuses the store, its timers and Toast.css as is; reports pause and resume like the React Toaster.

native.note: The same store. Safe areas and reduce motion from the platform.

styles.desk: Glass notifications as on the desk: strong glass fill, window blur, window radius and the soft window shadow (recipes/Toast.css). Solid under reduced transparency and more contrast.
styles.neutral: Planned: a white card with a small shadow.
styles.liquid: Planned: a glass capsule at the top center.

mistakes.right: An AlertDialog that says what happened and how to go on

mistakes.right: danger stays until closed; the store ignores a duration for it

mistakes.wrong: A toast with two buttons, or an action labelled OK
mistakes.right: One action at most, a verb plus a noun: Retry upload

mistakes.wrong: The same toast stacked five times by a retry loop
mistakes.right: Same copy, one toast with a count. Dedupe is on by default.

mistakes.wrong: A second Toaster for Arabic copy
mistakes.right: One Toaster per page; pass lang: "ar" on the toast

mistakes.wrong: A toast as the only place a result lives
mistakes.right: Show the result on the page too; the toast only says it happened

mistakes.wrong: Mounting the Toaster inside a dialog or outside the root Theme
mistakes.right: Mount it once inside the root Theme, before any dialog can open

mistakes.wrong: A dialog that closes when the person clicks a toast above it
mistakes.right: Call isInsideToaster(event.target) in the dialog's outside handlers and prevent the default

mistakes.wrong: toast({ type: "success", message: "Draft saved" }), or a toast component rendered by hand for a one off notice
mistakes.right: toast.success("Draft saved"), or toast("Draft saved", { tone: "success", lang: "en" }); keep the id to call toast.update(id, patch) or toast.dismiss(id)

name: Window
summary: An app window over the page: a title bar, a body and an optional footer. It opens from a trigger, moves, zooms, minimizes and closes. Desk draws it as a glass window with traffic lights; Studio as a flat panel with a close button.
useWhen: A tool or a document the person works in next to the page: a board, a file browser, settings
Several views the person arranges side by side and brings to the front
Content that opens from a control and should grow out of it
avoidWhen: A decision that blocks the page until it is made
A short message with no work in it
A list of actions behind one control
Content that belongs in the page flow

parts.WindowLayer: none: the positioned layer that hosts windows (data-ds window-layer, a region named Windows, النوافذ in Arabic). Not a part of a window; see a11y notes

kind.description: Sets data-kind. canvas: a large window with a margin of layer around it, no body padding. finder: wide, the layer edge around it. settings: centered, as tall as its content.

title.description: Names the window through aria-labelledby. One line with an ellipsis.

actions.description: IconButtons or small Buttons at the end of the title bar, before the window buttons. They are TitleBar parts.

footer.description: The footer part, for the window's Buttons.

open.description: Controlled open state, with onOpenChange. Keep rendering the Window with open={false}: it stays mounted while window-close plays, then renders nothing. Unmounting it instead (a conditional render) skips the close motion.

zoomed.description: Fills the layer. Sets data-zoomed and aria-pressed on the zoom light.

onZoomedChange.description: With it, or inside a WindowLayer, zoom works: the zoom light (Desk), the zoom IconButton (Studio), Enter on the move handle and a double click on the title bar.

minimized.description: Plays window-minimize toward the dock, then hides the window. Sets data-minimized.

onMinimizedChange.description: With it minimize works: the minimize light (Desk) or IconButton (Studio). The app shows the way back (a dock) and sets minimized to false.

frame.description: { x, y, width, height } in px: x from the inline start edge of the layer, y from the top. null lets the kind place the window. Controlled with onFrameChange.

onFrameChange.description: Called on every move by key or pointer, with the clamped frame.

movable.description: Drag by the title bar and move with the arrow keys. Default true inside a WindowLayer or with a frame. A Window outside a WindowLayer sits in the page flow (position relative), has no frame and does not move unless it gets a frame.

origin.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect the window grows out of and closes back into. Focus returns to it on close.

dock.description: An element, a ref or a screen rect a minimized window falls into. Default the bottom center of the layer. Focus goes to it when nothing before it in the focus order can take focus.

modal.description: aria-modal and a Tab loop inside the window. Off by default: windows sit next to the page.

closeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is إغلاق النافذة. A prop always wins.

minimizeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تصغير النافذة. A prop always wins.

zoomLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تكبير النافذة. A prop always wins.

controlsLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is أزرار النافذة. A prop always wins.

moveLabel.description: Name of the move handle: the title of a window that can move, focusable, a TitleBar part. Under lang="ar" the default is تحريك النافذة.

moveHint.description: Description of the move handle. Default names the arrow keys, Shift, and Enter when zoom works, in Arabic under lang="ar".

a11y.role: dialog, named by the title (aria-labelledby) or aria-label. Not modal unless modal is set.
a11y.focus: Focus moves into the window (the window element, tabindex -1) when it opens after mount, or on mount when its origin has focus. When the window closes or minimizes, focus goes to the first of: the origin, the next active window of the layer, the element that had focus before it opened, the dock, the WindowLayer (a region with tabindex -1). It moves only when focus was in the window or lost. Keyboard focus and pointer down both bring a window to the front.

keys.Escape: Closes the window. A control inside that handles Escape itself (a menu) prevents it first.
keys.ArrowUp: Moves the window up 16px, while focus is on the window or on its move handle (the title)
keys.ArrowDown: Moves the window down 16px, from the same places
keys.ArrowLeft: Moves the window 16px to the left on screen, in both directions
keys.ArrowRight: Moves the window 16px to the right on screen, in both directions
keys.Shift+ArrowUp, Shift+ArrowDown, Shift+Ar: Moves the window 64px, from the same places
keys.Enter: On the move handle: zooms the window or puts it back, when zoom works
keys.Tab: Moves through the lights or the title bar buttons, the move handle, the title bar actions, the body and the footer. With modal, Tab stays inside the window.

a11y.announce: The title is the accessible name of the dialog. The lights and the close button carry their own labels.
notes: Every drag has a key path (WCAG 2.1.1, 2.5.7): the arrow keys move the window from the window element or the move handle. The frame is clamped so 160px of the window and its title bar stay inside the layer.
Arrow keys pressed on a light, an action or anything in the body never move the window, so a roving toolbar in actions keeps its arrows.
Zoom has a key and a button in every style: Enter on the move handle, the zoom light in Desk, the zoom IconButton in Studio. A double click on the title bar is a pointer shortcut for the same action.
Moving is off while the window is zoomed, and for a window placed by its parent with no frame. The move handle is rendered only while the window can move.
Tab order follows the DOM order of the windows, not their stacking. Moving focus into a window with Tab brings it to the front.
A long title truncates with an ellipsis; the full text is the accessible name, and keyboard focus on the move handle wraps the title to show it in full.
No native title attribute.

WindowLayer is the container for windows, not a part of one: a positioned region (tabindex -1, named Windows) that stacks its windows, tracks the active one through the shared window manager and takes focus when its last window leaves. useWindowLayer() returns that manager, for a dock that restores minimized windows.

A Window outside a WindowLayer sits in the page flow (position relative), takes the size its parent gives it, has no frame and does not move. Give it a frame (and a positioned parent) to place and move it.
The five chrome labels (close, minimize, zoom, the controls group, the move handle) and the move hint default to Arabic under lang="ar", as Dialog and Toast do. A prop always wins.
Contract suite (many case, focus on the move handle): the arrow keys are checked with moves, Shift with the arrows with moves further, Escape with closes and Enter (zoom) with state-changes.

Arrow keys move the window in the physical direction on screen, in both directions: ArrowRight moves it right in Arabic too. A window is a spatial object on a desk, like a dragged card; a text or list control follows the reading direction, a positioned object does not (lead decision, wave 1).
Enter on the move handle zooms, and the handle is not rendered while the window is zoomed: focus moves to the window element (WCAG 2.4.3) and back to the handle when the window is restored.

native.note: Phones and tablets have no free windows. A native app shows the same content as a full screen or a sheet; see Dialog and Drawer.

styles.studio: A flat panel: the solid surface, the panel radius and shadow, no backdrop blur, a hairline under a plain title bar. No lights: minimize, zoom and close are IconButtons at the end of the title bar, minimize and zoom only when the window can do them. Open, close and minimize fade on duration.base; zoom has no motion.
styles.desk: A glass window: material glass with a 24px blur, radius 1rem, a hairline inside, the deep window shadow, a transparent title bar as in the source. The title bar starts with the traffic lights (optional part controls): idle dots at rest, colors and glyphs on hover or keyboard focus of the group. The window grows out of its trigger, closes back into it, zooms with a FLIP and falls into the dock. The layer carries the desk grain. In right to left layouts the lights stay at the top left and the title is centered.

name: WindowControls
summary: The traffic lights of a window: close, minimize and zoom. 12px lights with 24 by 24 px targets, each an IconButton with its own label.
useWhen: The controls slot of a TitleBar in a style that turns the window controls part on (Desk)
A window picture where the lights are shown but do nothing, with no handlers
avoidWhen: A panel in a style without lights (Studio)
Any control that is not close, minimize or zoom of a window

onClose.description: Without it the close light is disabled.

closeDisabled.description: With onClose: the close light is aria-disabled and data-disabled, stays in the tab order, blocks activation and draws as an idle dot; its glyph still shows on hover and focus. For a window or dialog that cannot be dismissed right now.

onMinimize.description: Without it the minimize light is disabled.

onZoom.description: Without it the zoom light is disabled.

closeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is إغلاق النافذة. A prop always wins.

minimizeLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تصغير النافذة. A prop always wins.

zoomLabel.description: Under lang="ar" the default is تكبير النافذة. A prop always wins.

label.description: The name of the group. Under lang="ar" the default is أزرار النافذة. A prop always wins.

active.description: data-state active or inactive, for hosts and recipes. As in the source, it does not change how the lights look.

a11y.role: group, named by label. Each light is a native button (IconButton).
a11y.focus: Each light with a handler is in the tab order with the 2px ring around its 24px target. A light with no handler is aria-disabled and out of the tab order (tabIndex -1): an accepted exception to the rule that disabled actions stay focusable, because a dead light is inert decoration of the window chrome; a screen reader still finds it, dimmed. A close light disabled through closeDisabled is an action that cannot run now: it stays focusable with aria-disabled, like any disabled Button.

keys.Enter: Presses the focused light. Nothing happens on a disabled light.
keys.Tab: Moves to the next light with a handler

a11y.announce: Each light is named by its label. The zoom light reports pressed while the window is zoomed.
notes: Never color alone: the glyphs (x, minus, arrows) show with the colors on hover and on keyboard focus of the group, and always in forced colors.
The lights do not mirror in right to left layouts. They keep the order close, minimize, zoom from the left, as macOS draws them and as the source does.
Targets are 24 by 24 px and touch, so light centers are 24px apart (WCAG 2.5.8).
No native title attribute.
